title: Populate remaining 11 DVB-T2 LDPC table data files
description:
## Goal

Populate the 11 missing DVB-T2 LDPC parity-check matrix source files
in `.txt` form to match the format of the one existing source file,
`crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/table_a_1_R1_2_N64800.txt`.

All 12 Rust constants are already in
`crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/dvb_t2_matrices.rs`; this task
provides the auditable source-of-truth from which those constants
were (or could be) derived, plus a parser-roundtrip test that
catches drift between the two.

## Context

Today only NORMAL_RATE_1_2 has its raw ETSI table committed as a
`.txt` source file. The other 11 configurations have Rust consts but
no source file documenting where the numbers came from. This makes
future audit / re-derivation difficult.

The format spec lives at
`crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/table_interpretation.md`.

The 11 missing tables, by ETSI EN 302 755 v1.4.1 Annex A name:

| Frame  | Rate | Suggested filename             | N      |
|--------|------|--------------------------------|--------|
| Normal | 3/5  | `table_a_2_R3_5_N64800.txt`    | 64 800 |
| Normal | 2/3  | `table_a_3_R2_3_N64800.txt`    | 64 800 |
| Normal | 3/4  | `table_a_4_R3_4_N64800.txt`    | 64 800 |
| Normal | 4/5  | `table_a_5_R4_5_N64800.txt`    | 64 800 |
| Normal | 5/6  | `table_a_6_R5_6_N64800.txt`    | 64 800 |
| Short  | 1/2  | `table_b_1_R1_2_N16200.txt`    | 16 200 |
| Short  | 3/5  | `table_b_2_R3_5_N16200.txt`    | 16 200 |
| Short  | 2/3  | `table_b_3_R2_3_N16200.txt`    | 16 200 |
| Short  | 3/4  | `table_b_4_R3_4_N16200.txt`    | 16 200 |
| Short  | 4/5  | `table_b_5_R4_5_N16200.txt`    | 16 200 |
| Short  | 5/6  | `table_b_6_R5_6_N16200.txt`    | 16 200 |

## Deliverables

1. 11 `.txt` source files matching the existing format.
2. A round-trip test in `dvb_t2_matrices.rs` (or a sibling test
   module) that parses each `.txt` file and asserts equality with
   the corresponding Rust constant — catches drift between the two
   in either direction.
3. Each new `.txt` file's header cites the ETSI EN 302 755 v1.4.1
   Annex / table number it comes from.

## Success criteria

- [hard] All 11 `.txt` files committed and parseable.
- [hard] Round-trip test passes: parsing each `.txt` yields the same
  table data as the corresponding Rust const.
- [hard] `table_interpretation.md` updated if a parsing rule is
  ambiguous against any of the new tables.

## Non-goals

- No change to existing Rust consts (only validation against the
  source).
- No change to LDPC encoder or decoder behaviour.
